subject: qilin
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: qilin, scaled hooved chimera with antlers and cloud mane.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a mythical qilin creature: a quadruped with a dragon head, antlers, scaled body, hooved legs, cloud-like mane details, flame tufts at the fetlocks, and a tail fan, standing on a small base, aiming for a large but efficient module of robust, untested code.

Now I'm designing the skeleton structure — hips, spine chain curving up to the chest, a neck curving to the head, and a tail chain extending backward from the hips — then setting up the body as a swept mesh following the spine bone chain with varying radii.

Simplifying the radius function with sine-based profiles for rx and ry, keeping round caps at the ends. Checking leg clearance against the body's belly, since legs run from hips down to hooves and the overall shoulder height needs to feel suitably tall for a qilin.

Now I'm estimating total height including head and antlers around 2.2 units, then working out leg geometry for each of the four legs using three-segment chains (shoulder-elbow-knee-fetlock style) with lengths that sum slightly more than the straight-line reach, giving a natural bend down to hoof height near the ground.

Defining the leg sweep...

With 3 segments reach checks out against the sum of lengths. I'm setting front leg bends with elbow back and carpus forward, and hind leg bends with stifle forward and hock back, mirroring deer anatomy. For the hooves, I'm thinking of cloven hoof shapes fitting the qilin's deer-like legs, built via a lathe or similar approach.

Now I'm building each hoof as a cloven split: two small cylinders offset on either axis with a gap between them to mimic the split hoof, positioned so the bottom sits at ground level with the ankle joint at the tip, plus adding fetlock tufts rendered as flame-shaped cards with gradient textures for extra detail.

I'm then planning the neck as a chain of points sloping forward and upward from the chest toward the head position, and sketching the head structure itself — a skull shape with snout, jaw, whiskers, antlers, fin-like ears, cheek frills, and eyes via decals, aiming for a stylized dragon-like qilin head with toon/cel shading.

For the body palette, I'm settling on a high-fantasy teal-jade scaled back, cream-gold belly, golden mane, and red flame accents, layering a scales effect inside the cel-shading function so both can coexist, with the mane rendered as an ethereal white-cyan-pink cloud gradient.

I'm planning the cloud mane as a combo of swirling ruyi cloud card textures along the neck and dorsal line plus clustered low-poly icosphere puffs for volume, both using the same cel coloring, and now tallying up texture needs: eye, cloud swirl, flame tuft, and cloud motif.

Beyond that I'm listing more surface textures -- a base ring, chest emblem, forehead gem, gold trim pattern, and plinth wave texture -- aiming for roughly 180+ parts total generated through loops. Now I'm setting up the color palette constants for jade, gold, cream, cloud blues, pink, and purple tones before writing the actual build code.

Deciding which kit imports to use, I'll stick with toon cel shading and glow for most paints, choosing cel-shaded gold over mixed metal styles to keep things simple. I'm building the scale paint for the back using a toon-cel wrapper around a layered scale pattern function with jade tones.

Then for the body coat, I'm using a countershade function to blend the back scales with a lighter cream-gold belly paint, applying it across the body and legs; for the legs I'm adding a zigzag-based threshold so the lower portion switches to a gold cel paint for a sock effect.

I'm settling on a paint texture size around 2048 for the detailed scale work, since the atlas should still fit comfortably alongside the other texture layers at 4096. Now I'm working out how to place the head joint using local forward/up/right offsets to position it correctly relative to the body.

Writing head geometry specs...

Adding whisker tendrils off the muzzle, then rigging a lower jaw joint with its own frustum box tapering toward the chin, plus small tooth cones and a hanging goatee tuft for detail.

For the nose I'm placing two dark nostril spheres with a pad, and for the eyes I'm decaling an anime-style eye texture onto the skull surface, computing hit positions by azimuth and elevation around the skull center so the eyes sit forward-facing but angled to the sides, sizing each decal to fit within the skull's scale.

I need to make sure the decal only samples the skull surface and not the muzzle box, and I'm mirroring the eye decal for the left side when s is positive. I'm also adding a swept brow ridge above each eye like flame-shaped fins, and widening the skull sphere slightly with bigger eye sizes for a more anime look before moving on to the ears.

Working out the ear geometry now, planning fin-like extruded leaf shapes angled backward at the sides of the head, with mirrored placement and flattened membrane thickness for a dragon-like look.

Then I'm moving on to the antlers: two branching gold antlers with jade glowing tips, built from a main curving beam swept via Catmull-Rom splines with three tines branching off, computed in head-local space.

Adding small glow orbs at beam tip and tine ends, computing tine direction by blending the path tangent with outward/upward/forward side vectors using Vector3 math, keeping antlers rigidly bone-bound to the head. Now I'm planning whiskers as long catmull sweeps flowing back from the muzzle sides.

For the forehead I'm adding a small glowing octahedron gem in a golden setting as a decorative jewel, and skipping a separate horn since the antlers cover that role. For the mouth I'm building a dark interior box between the jaw pieces and setting a slightly open rest pose on the jaw bone for readability.

I'm planning the jaw to open by angling it forward slightly, building parts onto it before posing so they inherit the rotation, and adding a dark reddish interior box plus a tongue for depth. With the mouth open about 10 degrees, fangs will read clearly. Now I'm shifting to the neck, building it as a chain of joints parented to the last spine joint, following a curved catmull-rom path upward from the chest toward the head.

I can reference neck.at(1) directly for the head joint's position rather than resolving the bone manually, and I'll set the head's orientation using the named direction words to avoid axis confusion rather than raw dir vectors.

For the mane, I'm placing icosahedron cloud puffs along the neck sweep's dorsal frame, using the sweep function to get position and orientation at each point so the puffs follow the tube's bending naturally, with radius varying along the sequence.

I'm defining a small palette of cel-shaded cloud colors—white, cyan, and pink variants with matching shadow tones—to randomly assign across the puffs, and planning the mane's path to run along the neck crest and continue down the spine toward the tail base.

Beyond the main crest puffs and smaller side layers, I'm adding flowing cloud tendrils and swirl-textured cards that lean back along the flow, plus spiral "ruyi cloud" motifs extruded at the shoulders and haunches as a decorative touch typical of qilin iconography. I'm working out a bumpy-circle outline generator to create these extruded cloud shapes using cosine-based radius variation for the lumpy edges.

Writing spiral sweep helper...

I'll fall back to hips when the bone is missing. I want gold swirl curls on shoulders and haunches for ornamental flair, plus a circular emblem decal placed on the flank, like a gold coin with a cloud swirl motif, mirrored on each side.

Now I'm designing a seal-like SVG medallion with a gold ring, jade center, cloud spiral, and red dot, then building the tail as a chain of points sweeping back from the hips into a flowing cloud/flame tuft made of overlapping blade shapes that gradient from teal to white.

Working out blade orientation math...

I'll define a reusable blade helper that extrudes a leaf-shaped outline (pointed sharp tip, smooth rounded base) scaled by length and width, which I can reuse across the tail tuft, fetlock flames, back crest, forelock, and beard for consistent 3D leaf-like geometry.

For color, I'm giving each blade a gradient by painting based on position along its length, blending from base color to tip color with banded toon-style transitions rather than a smooth gradient.

I'll round blade lengths to two decimals and cache paints in a map to cut down on duplicate creations. Now thinking through the leg details — knee and hock tufts, fetlock tufts angled back-down, dorsal ridge blades along the spine and tail base, and a stone plinth base with carved wave patterns, lumpy cloud puffs at the feet, a gold ring, and glowing jade orbs.

I'm figuring out the dais sizing so it covers the qilin's full footprint, adjusting the tail path to curl sideways rather than trailing straight back so it stays within the base radius, and checking that the head's forward reach and tail tip distances both fit within a slightly enlarged dais radius centered a bit behind the model's origin.

Now I'm working out the dais construction as stacked lathe tiers, and resolving the floor-contact requirement: since the whole model's lowest point must touch y=0, I'm treating the dais itself as sitting on the floor and adjusting the dais top height so the creature's hooves rest naturally on it without violating the "nothing sinks or floats" constraint.

Still setting up the dais bone...

I'll flatten the top tier so feet sit properly, then add a decorative outer rim ring with a raised gold torus-like edge. For surface detail, I'll overlay a circular seal texture on top with concentric rings and cloud/trigram patterns, sized to fit the dais radius just above the stone surface.

For props, I'm keeping it modest: a few cloud-puff clusters near the rim, small glowing crystal clusters at the rear-left and front-right, stone studs spaced along the rim loop, and cloud puffs at the base feet -- skipping any floating orbs to avoid gaps above the piece.

Now I'm moving to the rigged animal skeleton, starting to lay out the joint hierarchy from root through hips and spine.

Still defining joints and chains...

Defining the body radius function...

Still defining limb geometry...

I'll settle joint names: front legs use shoulder/elbow/wrist/foreHoof, hind legs use hip/knee/hock/hoof, keeping tips distinct. For the leg geometry, I'm sweeping a tube along each chain with a tapering radius array to get a smooth, natural leg shape from top to hoof.

I'm positioning the hoof as a split-cylinder pair near the ankle tip, cloven into two halves on either side of x, sized and colored to overlap cleanly with the fetlock tube, and considering adding a thin gold ring at the fetlock for accent.

Now I'm planning flame-tuft blades sprouting from the ankle in a flared, backward-pointing arrangement, colored in a fire gradient from deep red-orange at the base to pale yellow at the tip to evoke the qilin's flame-wreathed legs.

Still shaping the flame outline... Beyond that, I'm thinking the tail tuft should use the cloud-white-teal fan palette rather than flame, with the mane matching the cloud motif, and I'm starting to plan how cloud swirl cards wrap along the neck sweep.

For the cards along the neck, I'm pushing frames manually into an array inside the along callback rather than relying on an implicit return, since the callback's return behavior felt ambiguous. For lighting, I want the cards to use each frame's outward normal, so I'll compute side-layer frames manually off the sweep rather than relying only on the dorsal-facing default.

Now I'm sketching the swirl texture as a tall ruyi-cloud shape — a flowing lobed path with a white-to-pale-cyan gradient fill and soft blue stroke, plus an inner spiral line for detail.

Then I'm planning out the texture set for the decals: an anime-style eye with amber-gold iris, teal body, and a cute blush accent at the outer corner, followed by the cloud card texture, and considering whether a flame texture is even needed given the solid blade shapes.

I continue through the texture list, deciding to skip glint and fire cards for now and add a seal emblem plus a floor seal circle, while debating whether the chest needs a plate or cloud-collar trim decal (leaning toward skipping it). For the dais edge, I plan a glowing rune ring as a separate annulus plane layered over a plain stone floor texture, so the floor ends up split into two planes—one static stone base and one glowing rune overlay.

I decide to skip a forehead flame mark and instead add a tufted flame-strand texture for the beard whiskers and goatee tips, bringing my texture count to roughly six or seven: eye, cloud, seal, floor, runes, and tuft. I then start thinking through a gold collar necklace made of plates looping around the neck base, trying to work out how to position it using the neck joint's surface sweep and axis orientation.

Now I'm working out the necklace loop placement — using the surface sweep around the correct neck joint to avoid accidentally cutting the body tube, then adding a sweep of gold tubing with small octahedral pendants hanging along it, plus a front-facing gem pendant positioned at the belly-side angle of the neck curve. For the back, I decide the cloud puffs already handle the dorsal ridge and scales, so I move on to thinking about a forelock made from the cloud mane material swept forward over the forehead.

I'm also planning a mane across the top of the head with blades angled back-and-up, plus cheek ruffs of cream-gold blades at the jaw sides. Setting up the imports and helper utilities now...

Writing blade extrusion helper...

Since typecheck seems to actually run, I'll import the proper OutlinePoint type rather than fighting literal inference issues, and let the thickness taper from low to high y for the blade shape.

Bevel values must stay under half the thickness, and since the taper gets thin, I'll just skip bevel entirely to avoid validation failures and keep thickness as a plain number. I need to make sure the wind direction isn't parallel to the main direction, and flat shading should work fine with the blade's cel-style paint.

For coloring, I'm caching paint objects per blade keyed by palette and length, with a function that picks one of three palette colors based on how far along the blade's length a given point falls.

Now I'm working out the typing for palettes without importing SDK types directly, defining a Pal type as an array of cel results, and confirming the normalized position along the blade works correctly for the paint lookup regardless of smoothing. I'm defining the color palettes for different grass/mane elements—root-to-tip gradients like teal-to-cyan-to-white for clouds, teal-to-mint-to-white for tails, and starting on a blue-green mane palette...

I'm sketching a flame-rendering helper that layers multiple flat colors (red, orange, yellow) at decreasing scale to create a flame silhouette with a glowing effect, and thinking about how to offset the inner layers slightly along the thickness normal to avoid z-fighting between the colored flame layers.

For cloud puffs, I'm planning to use icosahedron geometry stuck onto bones with embedding and a flat-shaded flag to keep them matching the painted, non-glowing style of the rest of the model.

Since frame.moved returns its own frame, offset puffs should inherit the point's bone weights automatically, so anything stuck on a sweep point gets that point's skinning for free.

Now I'm building the body as a sweep along the spine, deriving the skin surface from that body, then scattering puffs along the neck and back using evenly spaced points with a defined range, skipping the overlap where neck meets chest. I'm working out the mane layout now, starting with the large crest puffs along the neck.

I'm planning the dorsal crest puffs with a shrinking radius toward the nape, side puffs set at angled offsets with smaller radius, and swirl cards along the dorsal ridge with lean, flow direction, and bend parameters for a textured mane effect. I'm also adding a tapering ridge of puffs and cards along the back, skipping the tail base cluster, and starting to define the neck sweep's radius function.

Now I'm thinking through the neck thickness tapering from a thick base near the body to a narrower top near the head, with the head joint positioned slightly forward of the neck's end and the skull radius sized to contain it. I'm sketching helper functions that convert local left/up/forward offsets into world points relative to the head's orientation, treating these as simple directional math on the head's local frame.

Adding dark ink nostrils, cheek flange pads, and fang cones for the snout details, then moving on to shaping the lower jaw.

Now adding teeth: small cone-shaped fangs on the upper jaw pointing downward and lower fangs on the jaw bone pointing upward, positioned near the mouth tips for a toothy look.

Writing whisker curves...

Defining the antler curve points, but reconsidering the height since 0.64 up would push the tip too far above the head for the body proportions — scaling it down so the tip sits around 0.5 up with a gentler backward curve instead.

Now I'm adding tines branching off the beam at several points along its length, computing each tine's direction by blending the beam's tangent with outward, forward, and upward vectors, then sweeping a tapered curved shape for each tine with a pointed tip and a small glowing jade orb at the end.

I'm also setting up the beam's radius profile and cap styles, planning a gold collar ring at the antler base, and defining a shared gradient paint (brown to tan) that both the beam and tines will use based on world vertical position for visual consistency across the antler.

For the ears, I'm planning leaf-shaped blade extrusions angled outward and back from the head, giving them a pale teal membrane with a smaller pink blade layered in front for depth.

Now I'm sketching the tail as a curved path tapering back and down into a tuft, where I'll fan out several blades at the tip following the tangent direction to create a brush-like end.

Still working out tuft geometry...

I'm checking the tail tip position and tuft overhang against the dais radius, adjusting the tail to curve more sideways so it stays within bounds. I also want to add seal decals along the body flanks.

Still placing decal positions...

Actually, reconsidering the approach—maybe instead of an emblem, I'll add thin gold trim lines running along the body's flanks at symmetric angles, swept as narrow tubes following the body's own path geometry.

I also want a gold girth band encircling the body at mid-torso, using a loop cut at the spine joint position so it wraps around the body cleanly without intersecting the legs.

For the pendants, since sticking cones along the loop points them tangentially instead of outward, I'm switching to small gold sphere beads instead, placed directly at frame points along the loop for a tassel-like decoration.

I'm trusting the girth band skin loop will work fine on the body surface since there's no risk of plane misses with a single body loop. For the chest collar, I'm using the neck's second joint position with a sweep plane facing along the neck axis, same approach as before — then moving on to hooves, dais, and base details anchored to the root bone.

For the dais, I'm lathing a tapered outline with a beveled edge, and coloring it with a mottled stone pattern wrapped in a cel shader so the lit top face reads properly. Now I'm starting a second, wider lathe shape for the lower base step beneath it.

Still writing lathe geometry...

Tallying up the element count across the whole piece — body, legs, hooves, rings, flames, mane puffs, head, antlers, tail, base decorations, seal, trim — I'm estimating roughly 250 individual pieces total. Writing seal SVG markup...

I'm also mapping out the texture set — EYE, CLOUD, SEAL, FLOOR, RUNES, plus extras like a chest medallion, a scroll trim decal for the collar, and small TUFT cards for beard and whisker tips. I'm adding a SPARK texture too, a four-point glowing star card for scattered sparkle effects.

Glow keeps the texture colors with no stroke. Now I'm checking the builder API details—paintSize for texture resolution, the spine sweep function with radius and shift parameters, and positioning the hips and chest regions relative to the spine's z-coordinates.

Working out the neck path now, starting it inside the chest dome and curving upward through several control points toward the head position.

Generating card placement code...

Defining color palette constants...

Defining leg sock paint...
